newsitem.title: UK: SNP support slumps 6 points, Labour up 6 in poll.
newsitem.headline: SNP support slumps 6 points, Labour up 6 in poll.

text.p: Nationalist support slumped six points to a five-year low of 20 percent as Labour jumped six to 52 in the first Scottish opinion poll since Prime Minister John Major set May 1 for Britain's general election.
Major's ruling Conservative Party gained one point to 17 percent, the best level for three years, in the System Three poll for the Herald newspaper on Wednesday.
Liberal Democrat support dropped one to nine percent.

Scottish National Party (SNP) leaders shrugged off the fall as a temporary result of last week's decision by the Scottish edition of the mass-selling Sun newspaper to ditch the party and support Labour.
At 20 percent, SNP support is one percent down on the party's vote in the 1992 general election.
Conservatives are below 1992's 26 percent and Labour well up on a 39 percent share five years ago.
Conservatives now hold 10 of Scotland's 72 seats in parliament. Labour has 49, Liberal Democrats nine, and SNP four.
